## Round 4: Verify with `check_cleaning()`

```{r}
check_cleaning <- function(before, after, orig_col) {
  new_num_cols <- names(after)[
    sapply(names(after), function(n) {
      is.numeric(after[[n]]) && (!n %in% names(before) || !is.numeric(before[[n]]))
    })
  ]
  if (length(new_num_cols) == 0) stop("No new numeric column found in cleaned data")
  if (length(new_num_cols) > 1)  message("Multiple candidates: ", paste(new_num_cols, collapse = ", "), " — using '", new_num_cols[1], "'")
  after_col <- new_num_cols[1]

  tibble::tibble(
    cleaned_col   = after_col,
    rows_before   = nrow(before),
    rows_after    = nrow(after),
    na_before     = sum(is.na(before[[orig_col]])),
    na_after      = sum(is.na(after[[after_col]])),
    values_before = dplyr::n_distinct(before[[orig_col]]),
    values_after  = dplyr::n_distinct(after[[after_col]])
  )
}

bind_rows(
  round_1 = check_cleaning(squirrels, clean_r1, height_col),
  round_3 = check_cleaning(squirrels, clean_r3, height_col),
  .id = "round"
)
```

Which original values ended up `NA` in your new numeric column? Replace `height_num` with the column the AI created.

```{r}
#| eval: false
clean_r3 |>
  filter(is.na(height_num), !is.na(.data[[height_col]])) |>
  count(.data[[height_col]], sort = TRUE)
```
